video.title: This Simple AI Setup Makes Me $8K Every Month

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates a business of AI Spanish video dubbing with lip sync for local businesses and creators. He uses OpenArt's Arena leaderboard to pick the top lip-sync model (Seedance 2.5), dubs his own talking-head clip and a farmers-market vendor clip in minutes, and lists five customer types to pitch. He sends one free-sample DM to a vendor (no reply) and claims dubbing his own channel into 13 languages earns about $8K/month extra ad revenue. Key takeaway: pick a niche, make free samples, and do high-volume outreach; the video is partly sponsored by OpenArt.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; dubs his own YouTube channel into 13 languages

ideas.name: AI Spanish lip-sync video dubbing for local businesses
ideas.one_liner: Dub small businesses' existing videos into Spanish with AI lip-sync and charge per video or monthly.
ideas.business_model: Per-video fee or monthly retainer for dubbed videos
ideas.customer: Local US businesses with video content: home services, dentists/med spas, real estate agents, food vendors and small restaurants
ideas.problem: About one in seven US people speak Spanish at home but businesses have no Spanish versions of their videos; traditional dubbing or re-shoots are too costly and lips don't match.
ideas.offer: Spanish-dubbed version of the business's existing video with matched lip movement, keeping the speaker's voice and pacing, delivered fast.

pricing.model: Per video (about $300) or monthly package for two videos
pricing.notes: Do first ones free for testimonials, then low-to-mid hundreds per video, or charge by minute/second for longer videos. Test pricing to find equilibrium.

acquisition_channels.details: Text/DM business owners with a free pre-made Spanish version of their video: 'I made a Spanish version of one of your videos for free. No catch. Want me to send it over?' then offer two a month for $500. Host's single DM got no response; expects single-digit to low-double-digit response rates.

quote.text: I was at the farmers market and loved it. I made a Spanish version of one of your videos for free. No catch. Want me to send it over?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Suggests 100+ cold texts and LinkedIn messages to find clients.

ideas.delivery: Operator uploads the client's video into OpenArt, picks the top lip-sync model from the Arena leaderboard (Seedance 2.5), runs a simple prompt to translate and dub into Spanish keeping voice and pacing, trims to about 30 seconds for ads, and delivers the output. Generation takes about 1-2 minutes.
unit_economics_claims: $300 per video, two videos a month gives $500-600 per client per month
10 clients at $500 a month is $5,000 a month
Task takes about 20 minutes or an afternoon
Token costs are a tiny fraction of the price charged
ideas.startup_cost: A few tokens/credits on OpenArt; no other cost stated

acquisition.how: Cold DMs/texts to local business owners (often sole traders) are restricted under UK PECR; outreach is mostly manual and low response; inbound content or ads could help but isn't described.

onboarding.how: Client sends a video file and approval; an agent can handle intake and forms.

delivery.how: A single prompt on a hosted model does the dub; an agent could upload, trim, generate and QA, with occasional human check of the Spanish quality and lip sync.

billing.how: Stripe invoices or subscriptions are easily automated.

support.how: Revision requests and quality complaints can be mostly agent-handled with human review.

uk_applicability.notes: The pitch relies on the large US Spanish-speaking population (44M); the UK has far fewer Spanish speakers, so the local-business angle is weak. Could be adapted to other languages (Polish, Urdu, Arabic, Gujarati) or to exporting to Spanish-speaking markets. DM outreach to sole traders has PECR issues.

risks: Dubbing quality varies by model and may produce mumbled or inaccurate Spanish; host cannot verify Spanish well
Cold DM response rates are low
Dependence on a third-party platform's models and pricing
Easy to copy; low barrier to entry
Voice and likeness cloning consent for client videos

ideas.name: Dubbing a YouTube channel into multiple languages for ad revenue

ideas.customer: YouTube viewers in other countries (and creators with 100K+ subs as a service customer)
ideas.problem: Videos only reach audiences who speak the original language.
ideas.offer: Multiple audio tracks per video via YouTube's audio track feature, opening Mexico, Spain, Colombia and other markets.

pricing.model: Ad revenue (about $8 per thousand foreign views, claimed)
pricing.notes: Also pitched as a service to YouTubers with over 100K subscribers.

acquisition_channels.details: Uses his existing channel's audience and YouTube's multi-audio-track feature.

ideas.delivery: Dubbing pipeline (custom app built by host, or OpenArt for a couple of clicks) produces audio tracks uploaded to YouTube.
unit_economics_claims: Over a million foreign views per month gives about $8,000 extra per month

acquisition.how: YouTube distributes dubbed tracks automatically to viewers by language.

delivery.how: Pipeline can dub and upload automatically; occasional quality checks.

support.how: Comment moderation is the only support.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same in the UK, though it requires an existing channel with large views.

risks: Lip match is lacking in YouTube audio-track dubs, as shown in Arabic

tactics.name: Pick the lip-sync model via the OpenArt Arena leaderboard
steps: Open the OpenArt Arena lip-sync leaderboard
Use the simple dub prompt keeping voice, pacing and lip match
Compare against a lower model only if needed

quote.text: Look at the board. The leaderboard. Run with the top model.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Free sample DM to get the first yes
steps: Find a local vendor's existing video
Dub it into Spanish for free
DM: made a Spanish version, no catch, want me to send it?
Offer two videos a month for $500 if it brings customers
If no reply, send the video proactively

quote.text: the magic of this DM is the word free. No one's going to say no to a free thing that's already made.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Choose a clip that shows lips and logo
steps: Trim the source video to about 30 seconds
Pick a segment where the mouth and logo are clearly visible
Prefer talking about the business over hard selling

tactics.name: Start with free work for testimonials, then test pricing
steps: Do first videos free for testimonials
Move to low-to-mid hundreds per video
Consider per-minute or per-second pricing for long videos

tactics.name: Niche down to an industry you know
steps: Pick an industry you have worked in (pizza, restaurants, oil change)
Pitch businesses in it using your insider knowledge

warnings.warning: A single DM won't build the business; the host's one DM got no reply, so volume outreach is needed.

quote.text: I did not get a response to that DM. So, I got to send more DMs.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Poor lip sync looks bad and clients won't want it on their website; model choice matters.

quote.text: When the lips don't match the words, it looks like a kung fu movie from 1978.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: YouTube's audio-track dubs don't match lips, which limits performance.

lessons.lesson: Use a blind-test leaderboard to choose AI tools instead of testing every model yourself; it saves time and credits.

quote.text: It's a taste test with the labels ripped off.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Do a small piece of work for free first so the prospect can see the result; free removes the objection.
With no testimonials, doing early work free to get social proof is worth it.
Test pricing until you find what people will pay; don't set it once.

quote.text: You really want to play around with the pricing of these videos until you find equilibrium
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pick a niche you know, since expertise helps with pitching and credibility.
Spotting an underserved segment (Spanish speakers) in a market where competitors have nothing gives an easy wedge.
Outreach is a numbers game; expect low response rates and keep sending.

quote.text: Shoot your shot over and over and over again.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Cheap tokens versus high-value deliverables make an asymmetric bet with low downside.
A skill that opens new markets for your own content can be a revenue source before selling it as a service.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly hypothetical revenue math for the service business; the only first-hand figures are his own channel's foreign-views revenue, which is unverified. The service has no real client results, and the only DM test got no response.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: OpenArt is a partner/sponsor of the show and the host uses it; also links a free doc and promotes his cold-outreach content.
